===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|Spam}}, {{l|en|SPAM}}

===Etymology===
The original sense ([[can]]ned [[ham]]) is a proprietary name registered by Geo. A. Hormel & Co. in U.S., 1937. It is presumed to be a conflation of either "'''sp'''iced h'''am'''" or "'''s'''houlder of '''p'''ork and h'''am'''"<ref>{{cite-web |title=What does the SPAM brand name mean? |work=SPAM |accessdate=6 July 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014172553/http://www.spam.com/spam-101/what-does-the-spam-brand-name-mean |archivedate=14 October 2013 }}</ref> but was soon extended to other kinds of canned meat. Hormel spells the trademarked name in all upper case.

The use for unsolicited and unwanted email derives from a {{w|Monty Python's Flying Circus}} sketch.<ref>{{cite-av|en|episode=Spam|date=1970-12-15|number=12|season=2|title=w:Monty Python's Flying Circus|mainauthor=w:Monty Python|writer=Michael Palin;Terry Jones|network=BBC One|publisher=BBC|location=London|url=http://us.imdb.com/title/tt0650991}}</ref> In the 1970 sketch, a group of Vikings in a restaurant repeatedly chant the word "spam". The earliest recorded real-life use for this sense occurs around 1993 which finds reference in a newsgroup post dated March 31, 1993, but the term may have been in use on "[[multi-user dungeon|Multi-User Dungeons]]" ([[MUD]]s) in the 1980s.<ref>{{cite-web|en|title=Origin of the term "spam" to mean net abuse|author=Brad Templeton|work=Brad Templeton's Home Page|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716231643/http://www.templetons.com/brad/spamterm.html|accessdate=2025-10-05}}</ref>

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|Q13512320}} {{lb|en|uncountable|rarely|countable|computing|Internet}} Unsolicited bulk electronic messages.
#: {{syn|en|junk mail}}
#: {{ant|en|ham}}
#: {{cot|en|bacn}}
#: {{ux|en|I get far too much '''spam'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I received 58 '''spams''' yesterday.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=No hiding place
|date=2013-05-25|volume=407|issue=8837|page=74
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no
|passage=In America alone, people spent $170 billion on “direct marketing”—junk mail of both the physical and electronic varieties—last year. Yet of those who received unsolicited adverts through the post, only 3% bought anything as a result. If the bumf arrived electronically, the take-up rate was 0.1%. And for online adverts the “conversion” into sales was a minuscule 0.01%. That means about $165 billion was spent not on drumming up business, but on annoying people, creating landfill and cluttering '''spam''' filters.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025020559/https://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no|archivedate=25 October 2017}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|computing|Internet}} Any [[undesired]] electronic [[content]] automatically [[generate]]d for [[commercial]] purposes.
# {{lb|en|Internet}} Excessive, often [[unwanted]] and repeated [[online]] messages.
# {{lb|en|Internet}} {{ellipsis of|en|spam account}}.
# {{lb|en|by extension|often|video games}} A large quantity or [[multitude]] of anything done repetitively or considered unusually or [[indiscriminately]] [[repetitive]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|computing|Internet}} To send spam (i.e. unsolicited electronic messages.)
#* {{quote-newsgroup|en|title=ARMM: ARMM: >>>>Ad Infinitum|newsgroup=alt.folklore.computers|author=Joel Furr|date=1993-03-31|id=d5SlxvmhmNwJ|url=https://groups.google.com/g/alt.folklore.computers/c/P3YNtAi7EJw/m/d5SlxvmhmNwJ
|text=Transformed by programming ineptitude into a monster of Frankenstein proportions, it broke loose on the night of March 31, 1993 and proceeded to '''spam''' news.admin.policy with something on the order of 200 messages in which it attempted, and failed, to cancel its own messages.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing|Internet}} To send spam (i.e. unsolicited electronic messages) to a person or entity.
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive|computing|Internet}} To send messages repeatedly, often with disruptive effect; to [[flood]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|by extension|computing|video games}} To do something rapidly and repeatedly.
#: {{ux|en|Stop '''spamming''' that special attack!}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Spam''' the Z key to get a speed boost.}}
